subject: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up  GPU configs, reserved size & throughput targets
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up - GPU configs, reserved size & throughput targets

Hi Emma - appreciate the clear recap and the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. High-level answers below; I'll attach a short estimate PDF with examples for 1B and 3B token profiles.

1) GPU recommendation:
- H100 (80GB) - best latency and throughput for large-context models and mixed request lengths, highest price but best perf per GPU for streaming workloads.
- A100 (80GB) - excellent all-around option; slightly lower perf than H100 on some kernels but often more cost-effective for seq-lengths under ~2k.
- L40s / cost-optimized - viable if you optimize for cost and can tolerate higher latency; not our recommendation for customer-facing, low-latency features.

2) Reserved capacity sizing (rough estimates, assuming mid-sized open-weight LLM, continuous batching + KV cache):
- 1B tokens/month: ~2-3 x A100 80GB or ~1-2 x H100 80GB (depends on sequence length & concurrency); targets ~150-300k requests/day.
- 3B tokens/month: ~6-8 x A100 80GB or ~4-5 x H100 80GB.
(Conservative estimates assuming sustained 24/7 baseline with headroom.)

3) Ballpark $/1M tokens (12-month commit):
- H100 reserved: $12-18 per 1M tokens.
- A100 reserved: $15-24 per 1M tokens.
- L40s / cost-optimized: $20-35 per 1M tokens.

4) Volume adjustments: caching repeated prefixes and batching short requests can materially reduce billable tokens and improve $/token. If you share p50/p95 request sizes and percent short vs long-form, we can refine.

Next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with infra (we have availability Wed/Thu).
- Send scoped pricing estimate mapping token volumes to GPU count and monthly committed price (attached).
- Optionally set up a 30-day Dedicated trial on a small reserved pool.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-pricing-estimate.pdf (contains the 1B/3B scenarios and unit economics).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marcus - helpful, thanks. Couple clarifications from finance/infra: 
- Our target SLA for customer-facing endpoints is p95 token latency <= 200ms and 99.9% availability. Is that attainable on the H100 reserved path you suggested?
- For burst behavior: we need headroom to handle up to ~800 rps for short windows (avg 100-200 tokens). Will the 4-5 H100 estimate for 3B tokens support that with autoscaling/burst?
- On the $/1M token estimates, can you confirm whether those assume any infra credits, e.g., marketplace fees or cloud infra pass-through? We want to model net vendor cost to our P&L.

If you can confirm these points we can loop in procurement. Also happy to take that technical deep-dive Wed at 10am PT.

- Raj
VP Engineering, Finlytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finlytics.com>, Emma Zhao <emma@finlytics.com>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up - GPU configs, reserved size & throughput targets

Raj / Emma - quick answers and confirmed next steps:

- SLA & latency: Yes, the H100 reserved configuration (4-5 GPUs for the 3B profile) is the path we expect to meet p95 token latency <= 200ms for short requests, assuming a properly tuned runtime and KV/prefix caching. We'll validate on the deep-dive and can provide observed p95 numbers from similar customers.
- Burst handling: recommended pattern is a baseline reserved pool sized for 24/7 usage and a burst/auto-scale pool (either on-demand or pre-warmed nodes). For your 800 rps short bursts, a 4-5 H100 baseline plus configured burst capacity should handle spikes without impacting p95 for most requests. We'll include an autoscale plan in the technical doc.
- Pricing assumptions: the $/1M token ranges I sent are vendor net prices (Redwood list with committed-discount applied). Cloud marketplace fees or third-party infra pass-throughs are not baked into that number; if you're running via a cloud marketplace there may be additional pass-throughs - we can produce a net-of-marketplace view for procurement.

I confirmed Wed 5/5 10:00am PT for the deep-dive with Aditya (infra). We'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: throughput validation, caching strategy, and trial setup. Looking forward to it.

Action items: I will follow up post-deep-dive with a refined pricing sheet and recommended commit size.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
